findings.reason: AgentTUI kept one Session after Session.run released its writer claim, so later sends silently failed session appends. The final controller retains the same Session state for context and cumulative token budgets, but lazily acquires a fresh writer claim immediately before each run and lets Session.run release it; it never reuses a released token.

The SSE parser only marked text deltas as response events and parsed only non-streaming tool_calls. It now accumulates fragmented tool calls by index and returns them only after complete JSON-object arguments decode; tool-only responses and usage terminal events no longer become malformed empty responses.

An early draft treated a usage-only choices=[] stream as a valid empty reply because usage set the event flag. The parser now requires observed text or a tool call; usage is merged into that result, while a stream with only usage is refused rather than persisted as an empty assistant turn.

A session append failure was swallowed by Session._record_turn and the TUI returned a plain successful reply. The TUI now detects the existing session_file=None failure signal, preserves the provider reply, appends an explicit trace-only persistence warning and records last_error.
Ruff 0.17.3 E9/F found an unused fixture local in the multi-tool stream test; removed it and reran lint successfully.

Fresh-context review found that discarding the released Session after every run also reset total_input_tokens/total_output_tokens, defeating max_session_tokens across TUI turns. The controller now keeps one Session state, lazily reacquires a fresh writer before each run, and releases it at run end; a regression proves the second request is refused before the provider when the cumulative budget is exceeded.

Fresh-context review found that two streamed tool calls with different indices could reuse the same id and both execute. Stream finalization now rejects duplicate ids as malformed_response, with a discriminating regression.

Exact-SHA review found that streamed usage:{} was reported as missing because usage_reported used truthiness, unlike the non-streaming contract. Streaming now tracks whether a usage object was observed and reports true for an empty object with zero counters; a discriminating regression covers it.

Exact-SHA review found that a complete tool-only stream without a finish_reason was labeled stop. The normalized result now defaults to tool_calls whenever complete tool calls exist and no finish reason arrived; a focused regression covers it.

Delta review found that the supposed Session-level streamed multi-tool test returned a pre-normalized dict and never exercised SSE parsing. It now feeds synthetic fragmented SSE through _stream_response, then runs the real Session tool loop and asserts the second provider request carries both results in index order.

Delta review found that the review record still reported the previous 1471-test run and older 48/93 focused counts after the new regressions. The current record now reports kernel 50, agent 94 and full suite 1473 for this final tree.
